item.title: Urgent structural, welfare, and safety complaint regarding a severe road defect located at the junction of Ashley Road and Crouch Hill, 19th September
item.description:
Dear Councillors and Highways Team,I am writing to log an urgent structural, welfare, and safety complaint regarding a severe road defect located at the junction of Ashley Road and Crouch Hill, specifically adjacent to my property at 45 Ashley Road (the corner house).There is a significant pothole/depression in the carriageway directly on the path of the W7 bus route. Every time a double-decker W7 bus passes over this defect, it triggers violent ground-borne vibrations that cause my entire house to shake.This issue is causing severe domestic distress. The vibrations actively wake and disturb my one-year-old child every night, and the sudden, violent rattling terrifies the pets inside my house. The ongoing situation is severely impacting our quality of life and well-being.Furthermore, as a corner property, the building foundations bear the brunt of these vehicle-strike vibrations. I am deeply concerned about the long-term structural impact on the building. This has escalated beyond a standard road maintenance issue; it is a high-frequency public nuisance causing secondary property distress and welfare concerns on a major bus route.Under the council's code for reactive maintenance, I request that this specific defect be inspected urgently and fast-tracked for an emergency patching repair to stop the structural shaking and restore peace to our home.I look forward to hearing from you regarding a priority inspection date. Kind regards Jamie
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Crouch Hill, Finsbury Park, Greater London
